completion_data.completion_summary: Created agent-system/extensions/rust/ (manifest, EXTENSION.md, README.md, index-entries.json, opencode-agents.json, research/implementation agents with a cargo check/clippy/fmt/test verification loop, two wrapper skills, one context README), registered it in the extensions README table and the agent-contracts lint in-scope list, and verified with lint-routing-wiring.sh and lint-agent-contracts.sh (both pass with zero new failures).

memory_candidates.content: When adding a new language/domain extension to agent-system/extensions/, prefer the python extension as the structural template over nix: python is the lean baseline (manifest, EXTENSION.md, README.md, index-entries.json, opencode-agents.json, 2 agents, 2 thin wrapper skills, 1 context README) while nix additionally carries an MCP server, settings-fragment.json, a dedicated rules file, and hooks -- only copy those heavier elements when the new domain has a genuine equivalent need (e.g. an established MCP server), not by default.

A new extension's manifest.json needs a `keyword_overrides` block (`{"<task_type>": {"keywords": [...], "aliases": []}}`) for /task to auto-infer that task type from description text -- core's task.md keyword table is hardcoded and has no row for extension-provided task types, so without keyword_overrides the new task type is only reachable by explicit task_type selection.
